sections.html:
Lehi sits at the northern end of Utah Valley in Utah County, covering about 28 square miles at roughly 4,561 feet. The population climbed from 19,028 in 2000 to 47,407 in 2010 and 75,907 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 95,313. The median age was 26.2 in 2020, and about 39.5 percent of residents were under 18, so family-sized houses are the norm. An older home in the original grid looks very different from a subdivision built a few years ago.

Winters are cold, with a January mean low near 16 degrees, and precipitation averages around 12 inches. Dry air does not spare water lines and older furnaces from the cold, and buyers notice both.

sections.h2: Old Lehi and the original grid
sections.html: Pioneers settled the area in fall 1850 at a place called Dry Creek, and Lehi City was incorporated on February 5, 1852. The town stayed small for a century, with a census low of 2,733 in 1940 and only 8,475 in 1990. The Lehi Main Street Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Lehi Roller Mills, built by a farmers' cooperative in 1906, appeared in the 1984 film Footloose. A house in the old core often has older wiring, older plumbing and unusual lot lines, so expect inspection questions that a newer subdivision home would not face.

Lehi shifted from farming to a technology economy. Micron's chip plant became IM Flash Technologies, and Texas Instruments announced its purchase of the facility in June 2021. Adobe, Ancestry.com, Vivint, Microsoft and Oracle also have a presence. Ancestry.com has been headquartered here since 2016, the first hospital opened in June 2015, and Thanksgiving Point draws about 1.45 million visitors a year.

Owners who bought during a hiring wave can hit a layoff, a remote work change or an offer elsewhere. Timing becomes the problem, since the mortgage payment keeps coming while the house waits for a buyer.

Interstate 15 passes through Lehi with five exits, which is why many households chose the city. The FrontRunner station opened on December 12, 2012, near Thanksgiving Point, and Utah Transit Authority runs local buses. A buyer's agent will price in the distance to an I-15 ramp or the station. A house far from the interstate may draw a different buyer than one near the Corporate Center on Traverse Mountain.

Alpine School District, which includes Lehi High and Skyridge High, will cease to exist in July 2027. Three new districts will replace it, and one is named Aspen Peaks. Check the boundary for the exact property with the district or the city before you tell a buyer which schools apply. Mountainland Technical College has a Lehi campus.

The Building and Inspections Department issues every permit, and open permits or unfinished work can delay a closing. Applications go through an online portal, and the current codes include the 2021 I-Codes and the 2020 National Electrical Code with Utah amendments.

  • Call 385-201-1035 to schedule an inspection, with at least 24 hours notice. Voicemail, email and online requests do not work.
  • Have the work ready first, because re-inspection fees apply if a project clearly is not.
  • Look up status by permit number, site address or subdivision and lot.

Lehi also runs a pressurized irrigation system that supplies untreated water for yards and city fire hydrants. A city ordinance bars irrigation water use after October 15, and owners turn the connection on and off each year. Buyers from elsewhere often ask how the yard is watered, so explain the connection and watering schedule up front. Lehi City is at 131 N 100 E, phone (385) 201-1000.

Utah County mails valuation notices in summer, sends tax notices in October and collects by 5:00 pm on November 30. Appeals go to the Utah County Board of Equalization through the Auditor at 111 S. University Ave, Provo, or by phone at (801) 851-8109, option 3. The deadline printed on your notice governs, and it has been September 15 on past notices.

A valuation notice is not a tax bill. The amounts due appear in the October notice, so a seller closing in the fall should ask the title company how that year's taxes will be prorated.
Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder in Provo. The fee is $40 per document, and a state change added $5 to county recording fees, so ask for the current total before closing.

sections.h2: Does the primary residence exemption follow the house?
sections.html:
No. Utah takes 45 percent off the market value of a primary home, leaving 55 percent taxable, and the owner must live there at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year.

After a sale or deed transfer, the new owner files Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. Counties cannot take late filings, and a buyer who misses the date can be taxed on full market value for that year. Rental owners file a residential declaration signed by all owners instead, and second or vacation homes do not qualify.

Telling your buyer about that date in advance avoids a surprise tax bill after a fall closing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Lehi
sections.html:
The title and recording steps are the same as in any sale, but the buyer needs no lender approval. A title company searches for liens, the parties sign, and the deed is recorded in Provo.

  • Tell the buyer about the house, its condition and your timeline.
  • Compare the offer and closing date with a listing plan.
  • Clear any open permits or liens before the closing date.
  • Sign and receive the proceeds after payoffs and prorated taxes.

This path suits owners who inherited a Lehi house, are behind on payments, or hold a house that needs work they do not want to finance.

A cash buyer needs no lender, so there is no appraisal gap and no list of repairs required by a bank. You do not stage rooms or hold open houses. The house is bought as it stands, including an aging furnace or an unfinished project, and you help choose the closing date. Any open permit still has to be cleared, so ask the building department what is on file for your address.

Unpaid taxes come out of your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for the balance and share it with the title officer. If the house closes in the fall, request the proration figure early, because the October notice changes the numbers.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lehi, Utah?
faqs.a: The estimate is 95,313 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 75,907, up from 47,407 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Utah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By 5:00 pm on November 30. The county mails tax notices in October, and a valuation notice is not a bill.

faqs.q: What is the Utah County appeal deadline for a Lehi property valuation?
faqs.a: Past notices have listed September 15. Check the notice you receive, since the date printed on it governs.

faqs.q: Will Alpine School District still serve Lehi?
faqs.a: Not after July 2027. Three new districts will replace it, so confirm the district for a specific address before telling buyers.

faqs.q: Who inspects building work in Lehi?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Inspections Department. Call 385-201-1035 at least 24 hours ahead to schedule an inspection.
